0.original: <hex:024804F201FC03><hex:024904F201FD03> Quest Sync<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103><hex:02100103>This creator recognizes you...or does he?

24.original: Deliver the nameless red fruit to the observers.

48.original: Azem? What in the blazes are you doing here?<hex:02100103>Hold on─ You seem...thinner somehow.

49.original: Hmm... You have much in common with <hex:02080DE905FF04686572FF0468696D03> but it's clear you're not one of us. A familiar perhaps?

50.original: I suppose it's just like <hex:02080DE905FF04686572FF0468696D03> to send one of <hex:02080DE905FF04686572FF0468697303> minions to poke its nose into our affairs. But since you're here, instead of hanging around like a bad smell, why don't you make yourself useful?

51.original: I want you to take this latest work of mine─a new variety of fruit─to my colleagues.

52.original: In the meantime, I will be cultivating more specimens in the Chthonic Horns. Yes, you heard that correctly. Cultivating, not simply conjuring with creation magicks. Aye, the fruit I produce is a labor of love.

53.original: Now that my newest masterpiece is close to completion, I would have my fellow researchers sample its delights. I wish to hear their impressions before I make the final adjustments.

54.original: Unfortunately, for all their wisdom, I find them intolerable at the best of times, never mind when they are critiquing my work. For that reason, I would have you go in my stead. And be quick about it─lest the fruit spoil as a result of your dawdling.

55.original: Yes? Is something the matter? I've already given you your instructions, and I'd prefer not to repeat myself. Now go.

56.original: You are the familiar who arrived with Emet-Selch and Hythlodaeus, yes? And what do we have here?

57.original: A new species of fruit, eh? Let us hope it tastes better than it looks.

59.original: What an unusual flavor! Equal parts bitter, musty, and tart...and not entirely unpleasant. I am curious to know how such a thing was created.

60.original: Grown from seed in the Chthonic Horns, you say? In my experience, leaving such things to nature leads to wildly varying results. To have bred such a specimen must've been incredibly time-consuming, not to mention inefficient.

61.original: You wish to speak with me?

64.original: It's so outrageously bitter, something akin to a wave of icy cold has spread throughout my entire body!

65.original: I certainly wouldn't eat this out of choice, but it could be made into medicine for staving off the heat in arid environments.

67.original: For me? Why yes, I should love to try a piece!

69.original: I don't mean to be rude, but this falls somewhere between “rather foul” and “positively revolting.” It's so bitter, it's practically inedible.

70.original: More important, however, is the question of whether this fruit would serve its intended function. If wild animals cannot bring themselves to eat it, the seeds will never be spread. I can't imagine this creation being approved in its current state.

71.original: You are returned, minus three fruit samples, I presume?

72.original: Is that so? Not one of them found it to their liking? They claimed my last attempt was too sweet, and now it's too bitter!? Honestly, the nerve of these so-called experts!

73.original: As they shall soon learn, I am not so easily deterred.

74.original: For my next creation, I'll cross-pollinate sour and sweet varieties, and see what they have to say about <hex:021A020203>that<hex:021A020103>!

75.original: I'll show them it's these “wildly varying results” that come from adherence to natural processes that have the power to defy expectations! And as the familiar of Azem <hex:020815E905FF0868657273656C66FF0868696D73656C6603>, I'm sure you can appreciate that!
